records.name: East Java
records.summary: Direction mixed: in February 2025 content creator Isa Zega became the first transgender detainee held in this province's women's prison (Lapas Perempuan Kelas IIA Sukun, Malang), after her file was declared complete on suspected defamation/extortion - a documented case of an authority placing a trans woman in a facility by identity rather than legal sex, contrary to the usual national pattern. Otherwise a conservative pesantren heartland with no other sub-national signal documented. Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Indonesia.

records.name: Sabah
records.summary:
The audited sources for Sabah document Malaysia's federal and state-level framework rather than the province itself: same-sex conduct is criminalised under Section 377A with penalties up to 20 years and whipping, there is no legal gender recognition, and state-level syariah enactments penalise male cross-dressing; a 2022 human-rights report (retrieved as a fetch-time summary) documents state-backed discrimination - arrests, raids and prosecutions driven by state religious authorities - across the federation. The source files state expressly that they contain no unit-specific findings for Sabah.

Sabah is therefore assessed on the national framework alone: criminal provisions apply through the federal penal code as in the rest of Malaysia, religious-offence jurisdiction exists at state level, and no audited source supports treating this province as materially safer or harsher than the federal baseline.
